data.gender_notes: Slavomira is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Feminine form of Slavo-mir, derived from the Slavic element slav-, meaning 'glory, fame, or fame' and mir, meaning 'peace'. The name Slavomira carries the meaning “Glory of Slav” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Slavomira usually hope their child will grow to embody glory of slav and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Saint Slavomira of Prague was a legendary Bohemian princess and martyr, said to have lived in the late 11th or early 12th century. She is believed to have been the daughter of Duke Spytihněv II of Bohemia and is known for her acts of charity and her devotion to Christianity.

Another Saint Slavomira is mentioned in the chronicles of the Hungarian Reformed Church of Transylvania. She was a Romanian princess, probably from Transylvania, who is said to have lived in the late 13th or early 14th century. She was noted for her piety, her generosity, and her devotion to the Christian faith.
